title: Send every field to the JSON partner unchanged

blocks.text: A partner processor takes your authorization requests and sends its answers as JSON over a socket, one object per message. Its system reads each object with an ordinary JSON parser and packs the fields for its own 1987 link to the networks, so whatever a field holds when it leaves you must be exactly what the partner's side reads, for every field a 0100 or a 0110 can carry. Both sides' test messages use the same kinds of value as production, including PIN blocks, chip data and merchant names as merchants type them.

`JsonPackager` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/JsonPackager.java` is a working `ISOPackager`: it writes one member per field and reads such an object back with a small JSON parser of the same kind the partner uses. Three methods are left, marked `TODO`:

items: `name`: the member name a field travels under;
`jsonValue`: the value written after the colon;
`put`: setting one member that was read back into the message.

blocks.text: The partner already sends text fields as members named by the field number, as the first test shows. About fifteen lines in total.

cases.says: a 0110 the partner wrote as JSON is read back with every field as the partner sent it
a message packed as JSON and read back keeps its card number, terminal and merchant
all-digit values keep their leading zeros: the MTI, the amount, the STAN, the approval code and the response code 00
a PIN block and chip data come back byte for byte, whatever bytes they hold
a merchant name with double quotes and a value with a backslash come back unchanged

origin.section: 16.2. JSON Has No Type for Fixed-Width Text or Raw Bytes

concepts: In JSON every field value travels as an escaped string and binary fields as hex, because numbers lose leading zeros and bytes put in as text are corrupted.
